headline: Google brought its Gemini assistant to Chrome on Android in India and turned on "auto browse", an agent that completes tasks in the browser, for paying subscribers.
score_reason: Clear product rollout with stated limits (English only, paid tiers for auto browse); it widens existing features to India rather than launching new ones, but the score is kept.
importance_line: Indian Android users get a free in-browser assistant and subscribers get an agent that can fill forms and place orders, with Google saying it asks for confirmation before sensitive steps, though those safeguards are Google's own claims.
summary: The Free Press Journal reports that Google has expanded Gemini in Chrome to Android users across India, months after the desktop version, at no extra cost and for now only on devices set to US or UK English; it can summarise pages, answer questions and use apps such as Keep and Calendar. Auto browse, which carries out multi-step tasks such as filling in a long form or placing a grocery order, is switched on for desktop and Android but only for Google AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers.
notes: Gemini in Chrome came to desktop in India earlier (months before); today extends it to Android and enables auto browse.
